What multiplication problem is represented by the model above?
question.worked_solution:
We have $\dfrac{1}{9}$ on the left and $\dfrac{4}{9}$ on the right.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129500/assets/eef3cec4311b03e7f4be59e367cbd3d6947afd73b16a00b487f28ae7ea2bf8b8.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\dfrac{1}{9} \times 4 = \dfrac{4}{9}.
$$

**Note:** We can swap the factors on the left-hand side. So, the following would be a correct answer too:

$$
4 \times \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{4}{9}
$$
